quote: No coward soul is mine, no trembler in the world’s storm-troubled sphere: I see Heaven’s glories shine, and faith shines equal, arming me from fear.
source: Emily Brontë, No Coward Soul Is Mine, lines 1 to 4, Wuthering Heights and Agnes Grey, with Literary Remains of Ellis Bell (1850)

evidence.where: Wikisource transcription of The Complete Poems of Emily Brontë (1908), which reprints Charlotte Brontë’s 1850 text with her headnote, checked against a second transcription labelled as the 1850 revision; the 1850 Smith, Elder volume itself was not viewed (archive.org reprints lacked the poems).
evidence.edition: Wuthering Heights and Agnes Grey, with Selections from the Literary Remains of Ellis and Acton Bell (Smith, Elder, 1850); text as reprinted in The Complete Poems of Emily Brontë (1908)

reason: Both witnesses print the four lines exactly as proposed, with the punctuation of Charlotte’s 1850 printing; the first stanza is the same in the manuscript and in the 1850 revision, so the wording is secure whichever text is taken. Not shipped, not banned, not at cap.
